Common questions about Meetily's attorney-client privilege protection, ethics compliance, and legal features

children.q: How does Meetily protect attorney-client privilege?
children.a: Meetily transcribes meetings 100% on the attorney's device using Whisper. There is no cloud upload of the audio or transcript by default, no third-party meeting bot joining the call, and no vendor-controlled data residency. Privilege stays within the firm because the privileged communication never crosses our infrastructure on the transcription path. If you choose a cloud summary provider (BYOK) on the Pro tier, only the transcript text you opt in to send is processed - audio and recordings always stay on the device.

children.q: Does a meeting bot join client calls or depositions?
children.a: No. Meetily captures system audio directly on the laptop. There is no third-party participant in the Zoom / Teams / Webex attendee list, which avoids both the optics problem (opposing counsel sees a 'Meeting Bot' in the room) and the privilege problem (a third-party processor receiving the audio stream).

children.q: What audit trail does Meetily provide for legal records?
children.a: On Community and Pro, recordings, transcripts, and timestamps are saved locally and can be archived under your existing matter-management system. On Enterprise, an admin dashboard adds centralized audit logs (who recorded what, when, on which device) and retention controls so the firm - not a vendor - decides how long material is kept and who can access it.

children.q: Is Meetily compliant with bar association requirements?
children.a: Yes, Meetily is designed to comply with bar association ethical requirements for client confidentiality and data protection. The local processing architecture ensures you maintain complete control over client communications and work product.

children.q: Can Meetily be used for client consultations?
children.a: Yes, Meetily is ideal for client consultations. It provides secure, confidential documentation while maintaining attorney-client privilege. The system handles initial consultations, client meetings, and case discussions with complete privacy.

Data sovereignty is maintained through local processing - all data processing happens within your own infrastructure, not on external servers. This ensures complete control over privileged communications and client information.

children.q: What security measures protect client confidentiality?
children.a: Meetily implements multiple security measures: AES-256 encryption, secure authentication, role-based access control, detailed audit trails, and automatic privileged communication detection. All processing happens locally within your secure environment.
